items.text: Marcus, 10 points off the lead, has Calafiori and Tzolis in his Arsenal corner, and the page is currently flagging Tzolis with a hamstring injury at 75% to play. Haramball Enthusiast kicks off Gameweek 6 hoping a hamstring reads the fixture list as generously as he does.

Manchester City have lodged an appeal against the independent commission's guilty verdict, calling it unsafe, and BBC Sport reports that without clarity on sanctions their ability to retain players and make signings is uncertain. City players with owners in this league: Edward has Semenyo, Justin has Haaland and Gvardiol, Marcus has Guehi and Foden, Small Ben has Donnarumma, Ben D has Matheus Nunes and Robert has Cherki, Ndiaye and O'Reilly. BBC Sport notes Nunes is one of four City players with a contract expiring within two summers.

source.title: What does Man City guilty verdict mean for their squad?

items.text: Liverpool v Man City is still to come, and it is a neat way to see who is exposed. Small Ben has Szoboszlai, Isak, Gakpo and Virgil on one side and Donnarumma and Ruben on the other, so he cannot lose the afternoon and cannot win it either, which is the only kind of hedging this league allows. Justin has Haaland and Gvardiol over there, and Big Ben has Wirtz facing Enzo and Matheus N., so he can at least cheer for himself.

Ten fixtures are still to come, nobody in the league has kicked a ball in the new gameweek, and Robert is 89 behind Edward. That makes this the one weekend where his team name, Pardinho, gets to be a joke and not a cry for help. He has Cherki and Ndiaye lined up against Liverpool and a whole lot of Arsenal and Chelsea waiting on a result, so there is a plot. It is a long way from a plot that gets him to the top.

The Premier League says its two leading scorers, Erling Haaland on five goals and Alexander Isak on four, go head-to-head when leaders Manchester City visit Liverpool on Sunday 11 October. Haaland is Justin's and Isak is Small Ben's, so the two of them will be watching the same match for different reasons.

source.title: When does the Premier League return?

items.text: The league resumes on Saturday 10 October with Arsenal, beaten 3-0 at Brighton before the break, at home to unbeaten Leeds, and Manchester United hosting bottom club Tottenham in the late game, the Premier League reports. At Old Trafford, Justin's Van Hecke and Marcus's Kinsky are in the Tottenham camp, with Edward's Lammens, Small Ben's Cunha and Big Ben's Bruno Fernandes among the United owners.

source.title: When does the Premier League return?

items.text: Coventry City, who recorded their first win and points of the season at Nottingham Forest, host Newcastle on Monday 12 October, the Premier League notes. Edward owns Forest's Murillo, Williams and Gibbs-White; Small Ben owns Newcastle's Hall, Barnes and Botman, and Big Ben has Thiaw.

source.title: When does the Premier League return?

items.text: Edward leads on 259 and owns neither of the league's two leading scorers: Haaland is Justin's, 7 back, and Isak is Small Ben's, 13 back. Return of the Djedi is top of the table with Semenyo and a lot of defenders, which is either a masterclass or the longest-running bit of luck in the league, and the six of you get to find out which when the break ends.

Erling Haaland asked to be substituted after 67 minutes of Norway's 2-1 Nations League defeat by Portugal on Sunday, with no word afterwards on his fitness. He was replaced by Jorgen Strand Larsen, so both are Justin's, and Manchester City visit Anfield on Sunday 11 October.

source.title: Erling Haaland injury fear after asking to be substituted for Norway

items.text: Alexander Isak left the Sweden squad with what Liverpool called a minor injury, and Cody Gakpo's break ended after 17 minutes against Serbia with an ankle problem, per the Dutch FA. Both are Small Ben's, and Liverpool host Manchester City on 11 October.

source.title: Cody Gakpo returns to Liverpool after injury for Netherlands

items.text: Kai Havertz went off in Germany's 1-1 draw with the Netherlands and has gone back to Arsenal for treatment, the knock understood to be a minor muscle strain. Big Ben owns him, and Arsenal are at home to Leeds on Saturday 10 October.

source.title: Kai Havertz returning to Arsenal to be assessed after suffering injury for Germany against Netherlands

items.text: Bournemouth's Alex Scott picked up a quad injury on his first England start in the 7-0 win in Croatia and has gone back to his club, with media reports suggesting he could be out for up to two months. Justin owns Scott. Ezri Konsa, Ben D's, also withdrew from the England squad with what is believed to be a minor issue.

source.title: Internationals: Which Premier League stars are shining - and who's got injured?

items.text: Man City's Nico O'Reilly withdrew from the England squad after playing just one match, while Arsenal's Bukayo Saka scored twice in the 7-0 win in Croatia. Robert owns both.

source.title: Internationals: Which Premier League stars are shining - and who's got injured?

items.text: Ben D is 40 off the lead in a team called Quantum of Tzolis, and Tzolis plays for Marcus. Ben D himself owns Havertz, reportedly out for four weeks, and Konsa, who has pulled out of England duty. Bold branding for a man who cannot keep his own Arsenal players upright.

Small Ben runs a team called Delap Dance, and Delap is in Ben D's squad. Small Ben owns Isak and Gakpo, both sent home from international duty with injuries, and he is 13 off the lead with Liverpool v Man City to come. The dance is looking like a limp.

Saka scored twice for England and Robert owns him. Robert is still 89 points off the lead on 170, because England goals score nothing in this league, and O'Reilly has gone home after one match. Pardinho: a fine name for a team whose best week happened somewhere it cannot score.

Man City have lodged their appeal against the independent commission's guilty verdict on Premier League financial rule breaches, saying the ruling contains "clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe". All six managers own City players, from Haaland (Justin) to Cherki (Robert), so nobody in this league is a neutral.

source.title: Man City confirm appeal against guilty verdict

items.text: Liverpool host Man City on Super Sunday, with Sky Sports assessing new Reds boss Andoni Iraola's early impact at Anfield ahead of it. Small Ben has the most riding on both sides of it, with Isak, Gakpo, Szoboszlai and Virgil for Liverpool and Donnarumma and Ruben for City.

source.title: Liverpool: Andoni Iraola's early impact at Anfield assessed ahead of huge Super Sunday showdown with Man City

items.text: Gameweek 6 has ten fixtures and not one has kicked off, so tonight's table is the last honest one for a while: Edward on 259, Justin 7 back, Marcus 10 back, Small Ben 13 back. Four managers inside 13 points, which is the most fragile kind of peace, and Robert is 89 behind on 170 and watching it from a different postcode.

Portugal boss Jorge Jesus revealed that Bruno Fernandes had been playing through pain during the international break. That is Ben D's Manchester United man, and nothing in the report says he is out of Saturday's game.

source.title: Player welfare, injury worries & boredom - has extended break worked?

items.text: Cole Palmer withdrew from the England squad, and BBC Sport says that has let others cement their place in front of him, with Morgan Gibbs-White cutting short a family holiday to join up after initially being left out. Edward owns both of them.

source.title: Midfield options and a fab front four - what we've learned about England

items.text: Chelsea's Morgan Rogers is part of the England front four BBC Sport rates after the break, while Declan Rice is out of the side as his load is managed after injury. Rogers is Ben D's; Rice is Small Ben's.

source.title: Midfield options and a fab front four - what we've learned about England

items.text: Edward leads on 259 with Justin on 252, Marcus on 249 and Small Ben on 246: thirteen points separate first from fourth, and ten fixtures kick off tomorrow with nobody having scored a thing. Robert is 89 back, which is nearly seven times that gap, so he is not so much in the title race as watching it from the car park.

Gameweek 5 left Justin's bench on 21 against 41 from his eleven, which is half a second team doing the work of the first. Robert's bench scored 0, so at least one of them is consistent. Both have the same ten fixtures to fix it tomorrow.

Declan Rice is close to agreeing a new long-term Arsenal contract, BBC Sport reports, and is expected to be involved when Arsenal host Leeds on Saturday at 12:30 BST. He is in Small Ben's squad; Edward has Calvert-Lewin on the Leeds side of that fixture.

source.title: Rice close to agreeing new Arsenal deal

items.text: Mikel Arteta has signed a new contract with Arsenal running until 2030, calling it 'only the beginning' of what the club can achieve. Every one of the six squads holds an Arsenal player, so nobody in this league gets to be neutral about it.

source.title: Arteta signs new contract with champions Arsenal

items.text: Chelsea's Morgan Rogers, on Ben D's squad, faces Bournemouth at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, the club where BBC Sport says he had an underwhelming Championship loan. Justin (Scott, Tavernier) and Marcus (Evanilson) own Bournemouth players in the same fixture.

source.title: £117m Rogers failed at Bournemouth - and feared he may not make it

items.text: Small Ben runs a team called Delap Dance, and Delap is in Big Ben's squad, where he returned 1 point in Gameweek 5. Big Ben's team is Quantum of Tzolis, and Tzolis sits in Marcus's squad on 2. Between them the two Bens have named their teams after footballers they do not own.

Robert is on 170, 89 behind Edward, after a Gameweek 5 of 22 points. None of the ten Gameweek 6 fixtures has kicked off, so for now Pardinho has not been outscored by anyone this week. Enjoy it, Robert; it ends at the first whistle.

Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo both picked up injuries on international duty with Sweden and the Netherlands, the Guardian reports, ahead of Liverpool's game against Man City. Small Ben owns both, along with Szoboszlai and Virgil.

source.title: Havertz, Isak, Dorgu ... spate of injuries with national teams leaves sour taste for top clubs

items.text: Christos Tzolis injured a hamstring playing for Greece and Kai Havertz suffered a similar problem with Germany, per the Guardian, while Martin Odegaard got 'nothing dramatic' on his X-ray after a heavy challenge with Norway. Marcus owns Tzolis, Ben D owns Havertz and Edward owns Odegaard.

source.title: Havertz, Isak, Dorgu ... spate of injuries with national teams leaves sour taste for top clubs

items.text: Bournemouth's Alex Scott is out for up to two months after getting hurt on England duty, the Guardian reports, a blow to a side still searching for a first Premier League win. Justin owns him.

source.title: Havertz, Isak, Dorgu ... spate of injuries with national teams leaves sour taste for top clubs

items.text: Sunderland will be without Brian Brobbey and Dan Ballard, who both strained hamstrings on international duty, according to the Guardian. Marcus and Robert each have a Sunderland player, and the team face Brighton this weekend.

source.title: Havertz, Isak, Dorgu ... spate of injuries with national teams leaves sour taste for top clubs

items.text: BBC Sport says Ezri Konsa has a slight niggle from England camp, that Cristhian Mosquera is fit and that William Saliba is on the mend with no clear return date. Ben D owns Konsa and Robert owns Mosquera.

source.title: What to do with Joao Pedro? FPL gameweek six dilemmas

items.text: Big Ben named his team Quantum of Tzolis, and the real Christos Tzolis is in Marcus's squad with a hamstring injury and an expected return of 24 Oct. Big Ben has built an entire identity around a player he does not own, who is not playing, and who is not coming back for a fortnight. Gameweek 6 has ten fixtures and not one has kicked off.

Carlos Baleba, the Brighton midfielder Manchester United signed on 25 August, could make his debut against Tottenham this afternoon, the Guardian reports, with United 12th after one win in their first five games. It touches Edward's Lammens, Marcus's Mbeumo, Big Ben's Bruno Fernandes and Robert's Yoro and Sesko, all in the XI that has to stop the leaking.

source.title: Will Carlos Baleba fix Manchester United? Three big questions ahead of potential debut

items.text: BBC Sport's FPL writer says Joao Pedro's fitness is in question for Chelsea's home game with Bournemouth, and that the Chelsea attack suffered without him against Brentford in Gameweek 5. Marcus owns him, and Robert has Chelsea's Estevao and James.

source.title: What to do with Joao Pedro? FPL gameweek six dilemmas

items.text: The Guardian's weekend preview asks whether Manchester City can summon a siege mentality at Anfield, with the club's charges row hanging over the trip. Justin has Haaland and Gvardiol, Edward has Semenyo, and Small Ben's Liverpool players are on the other side of it.

source.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend

items.text: Team news, Man United v Spurs (17:30 BST): Robert has Yoro and Solanke starting, but Sesko is not in the squad. Justin has Van Hecke starting, Marmoush on the bench. Marcus has Mbeumo and Kinsky starting. Big Ben has Fernandes starting. Small Ben has Cunha starting.

source.title: Confirmed line-ups | Man United vs Spurs

items.text: Chelsea led Bournemouth 2-0 after three minutes through Jordan Henderson and Morgan Rogers, then added João Pedro after the break, and Evanilson got the consolation, ESPN reports. That is Rogers for Big Ben and Joao Pedro and Evanilson for Marcus, who had both sides of the one game.

source.title: Chelsea 5-1 Bournemouth: Premier League result, goals and reaction - as it happened

items.text: Marcus is on 57 for the gameweek with three of his eleven still to play, and De Cuyper's 15 and Joao Pedro's 12 are doing the heavy lifting. Haramball Enthusiast sounds like a man who likes his football ugly, and he is winning it the pretty way, 28 clear of Edward.

Robert is on 9 for the gameweek and 127 behind the leader on the live feed, a gap you could park a whole Pardinho in. Saka and Gabriel played 90 minutes each for 2 points apiece, so his Arsenal contingent has been purely decorative. Four of his eleven have not kicked off, which is the only reason this is not yet an obituary.

Liverpool v Man City is still to come, and it is the one fixture all six managers own a piece of: Haaland and Gvardiol for Justin, Donnarumma and Ruben plus four Liverpool men for Small Ben, Foden and Guehi for Marcus, Semenyo for Edward, Enzo for Big Ben and three City players for Robert. Anfield is effectively playing the whole league, and nobody gets to sit this one out.

Arsenal defender Piero Hincapie was carried off during the warm-down after coming on as a late substitute in the win over Leeds, and BBC Sport says it raises concern he has an injury. All six managers own an Arsenal player, so the club's fitness list is everybody's business.

source.title: Hincapie injury adds to Arsenal issues after Guimaraes rescue act

items.text: Cole Palmer has signed a new Chelsea contract on improved terms until 2034, BBC Sport reports. Edward owns him and Marcus owns Joao Pedro, who the BBC also lists among the few Premier League players contracted to 2034 along with Haaland, who is Justin's.

source.title: Palmer signs new Chelsea contract until 2034

items.text: Manchester United led Spurs through Bryan Mbeumo's opener and then watched Rodrigo Bentancur get sent off for a headfirst charge at Luke Shaw, only for Spurs to equalise in added time through Solanke, BBC Sport reports. Marcus owns Mbeumo and Robert owns Solanke, so the draw gave each of them something.

source.title: Boos, anguish & fading belief - 'worrying day' for under-pressure Carrick

items.text: Team news, 13:00 kick-offs: Crystal Palace's confirmed eleven is out. Justin's Strand Larsen and Edward's Khalaili both start; Robert's Mateta is not in the matchday squad. Teamsheets for Forest, Hull and Everton were not available when checked, so Ben D, Small Ben, Marcus and the rest of Edward's and Justin's players are not covered yet.

source.title: Team News: One change for Palace against Forest

items.text: Team news, Liverpool v Man City (15:30 UTC). Liverpool's confirmed XI: Marcus has Alisson starting, Big Ben has Wirtz, Justin has Barcola, and Small Ben has Van Dijk starting but Gakpo, Szoboszlai and Isak are not in the matchday squad. City's teamsheet could not be read from a permitted source in time, so no City players are covered.

source.title: Confirmed Liverpool line-up v Manchester City

items.text: Marcus went into the day on 249, ten behind Edward on 259. All eleven of his starters have now played and none has blanked: De Cuyper 15, Dewsbury-Hall 13, Joao Pedro 12. He is on 326 to Edward's 298, 28 clear, with Edward holding one yet to kick off. Meanwhile Big Ben's team is called Quantum of Tzolis and Tzolis is on Marcus's list, on 0. Marcus will be mentioning all of this by breakfast.

Small Ben owns Szoboszlai, Isak, Gakpo and Virgil, and the squad list has all four on 0. Cunha's 10 and Rice's 7 are carrying a 27-point day, he is on 273 and 53 behind Marcus, and two of his eleven have not kicked off yet. That is not a Liverpool stack, it is a charity subscription.

Robert is on 195, 131 behind Marcus, with 25 for the day: eight of his eleven scored, three played and returned nothing, and none are still to come. Cherki's 10 is 10 of the 25, so the rest of the squad combined for 15. At 131 behind he is no longer chasing the leader, he is chasing the tail lights and the leader has fog lamps.

Manchester City ran over a ten-man Liverpool at Anfield after Ryan Gravenberch's second yellow card in the 62nd minute, with Rayan Cherki scoring the third, the Guardian reports. City keep their 100% start to the season. Robert owns Cherki, and Small Ben, Marcus, Big Ben and Justin each have a Liverpool player to explain.

source.title: Cherki cracker caps Manchester City win at Liverpool in face of Anfield taunts

items.text: Ipswich came from behind to beat Fulham, with Abdoul Ouattara levelling in the 88th minute and Dara O'Shea heading the winner in stoppage time, the Guardian reports. Fulham are winless in six and bottom of the table. Marcus, Edward and Big Ben all own Fulham players, and Small Ben has Ipswich's Davis and Enciso.

source.title: Ipswich stun Fulham with last-gasp comeback to increase heat on Arbeloa

items.text: Hull and Everton drew in a seesaw game, with Mohamed Belloumi earning Hull the point, the Guardian reports. Everton men on the books: Dewsbury-Hall for Marcus, Tarkowski, Garner and Barry for Edward, Pickford for Justin. Justin also has Hull's Ajayi, so he is on both sides of it.

source.title: Mohamed Belloumi grabs point for Hull in seesaw draw with Everton

items.text: Team news, Coventry v Newcastle (20:00 BST): all four league players are starting. Edward: Hornicek. Big Ben: Thiaw. Small Ben: Hall and Wissa. Nobody in the league owns a Coventry player.

source.title: Confirmed line-up: One change for Coventry clash

items.text: Coventry beat Newcastle 4-1, with Newcastle goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek spilling a ball and giving away a penalty in the fourth minute, which Jack Rudoni scored, ESPN reports. Edward owns Hornicek, Big Ben has Thiaw, Small Ben has Hall and Wissa.

source.title: Coventry put four past Newcastle to climb out of relegation zone

items.text: Marcus 77, Edward 39 for the week, and the lead is now 28. De Cuyper 15, Dewsbury-Hall 13 and Joao Pedro 12 did most of that for Marcus, while the best Edward could find was Jackson's 9. Edward went into Monday ahead by ten. Bonus points are still to be added, but nobody is expecting a rescue.

Newcastle lost 4-1 and managed to splash the misery across three squads: Edward's goalkeeper gifted a penalty, Big Ben's Thiaw and Small Ben's Hall played 90 minutes between them for nothing, and Wissa's 2 is the only thing resembling a return. A rare league-wide act of unity, and nobody wanted to be part of it.

Big Ben's team is called Quantum of Tzolis, and the Tzolis in question sits in Marcus's squad. Big Ben is fifth on 254, 72 behind the man who actually owns him. A team name that is mostly a monument to somebody else's player.

Crystal Palace came from behind to beat Nottingham Forest 3-1 at Selhurst Park, the Guardian reports: Dan Ndoye scored inside three minutes after a weak header by Edward's Anan Khalaili, then Daichi Kamada, Jefferson Lerma and Yeremy Pino turned it round. Edward's Morgan Gibbs-White, Small Ben's Daniel Munoz, Big Ben's Liam Delap and Justin's Jorgen Strand Larsen were all in it; Delap missed a golden chance from three yards at 1-0.

source.title: Pino finishes off Nottingham Forest on Glasner's unhappy Crystal Palace return

items.text: Ten-man Brighton won at Sunderland, the Guardian reports, with Maxim De Cuyper (Marcus) sliding in the first goal from a Pascal Gross (Big Ben) through ball in the 53rd minute and Jaouen Hadjam adding a second. Pascal Struijk was sent off after a VAR review, and Brighton stay third on 13 points. Justin's Enzo Le Fee supplied the best deliveries of a cagey first half but faded badly in the second.

source.title: Ten-man Brighton continue fine form with battling win at Sunderland

items.text: Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso admitted that Cole Palmer's decision to sit out the international break was related to last season's groin pain, the Guardian reports. Palmer (Edward) looked free-moving in Saturday's win over Bournemouth, setting up Jordan Henderson's opener inside 68 seconds, and has signed a contract running to 2034.

source.title: Henderson and Joao Pedro lead Chelsea charge against Bournemouth

items.text: GW6 is in the books and Marcus sits on 326, 28 clear of Edward on 298, with Justin a further 8 back on 290. Ten fixtures of GW7 are still to come and nobody has kicked a ball, so for one night only the leader is unbeaten, unbothered and presumably already drafting his acceptance speech.

Big Ben left 12 points on his bench in GW6, against 35 from his eleven, which is a rather large second team for a man on 254 and 72 behind. Robert, meanwhile, is on 205 and 121 off the lead: the gap is now wide enough to have its own postcode.

Manchester United striker Benjamin Sesko has a fresh shin injury with no end date, BBC Sport reports, extending a lack of involvement that the piece says United are keenly feeling. That is Robert's Sesko, who was already left out of the squad against Spurs.

source.title: Is Man Utd's Fernandes issue a symptom or reason for their form?

items.text: Michael Carrick says Bruno Fernandes is "pretty much over" the issue he was carrying on international duty and was "really bright in training", BBC Sport reports. Fernandes has played every minute of United's six league games, and Big Ben, who owns him, will be hoping the chance creation picks up from the 2.5 per game BBC quotes.

source.title: Is Man Utd's Fernandes issue a symptom or reason for their form?

items.text: Mikel Arteta called it "far from ideal" that Piero Hincapie and Martin Zubimendi were both hurt in a post-match training session after the win over Leeds, with scans due to give a timeframe, BBC Sport reports. Neither is owned in the league, but all six managers hold Arsenal players.

source.title: Hincapie and Zubimendi injured in post-match training session

items.text: Liverpool are now without a win in five successive Premier League home games (D4 L1) after the 3-0 defeat to Manchester City, BBC Sport reports, with Andoni Iraola saying his side played "two different games" either side of the red card. Small Ben owns Virgil, Gakpo, Szoboszlai and Isak, Big Ben has Wirtz, Justin has Barcola and Marcus has Becker.

source.title: Winless and an 'easy touch' - what's happened to the Anfield fear factor?

items.text: Small Ben named his team Delap Dance, and Delap is on Big Ben's squad, where he returned 2 in GW6. Small Ben sits on 281, 45 behind Marcus, with Virgil, Gakpo, Szoboszlai and Isak all showing 0 on his squad sheet. It is a team named after a man he does not own, held together by four Liverpool players who did nothing.

Justin is on 290, 36 behind Marcus, and left 7 points on his bench in GW6 while Haaland returned 6. His bench has therefore out-scored his centre-forward, which is the sort of thing a man with a team called Schwaddy should have noticed before Wednesday night.

Robert is on 205, which is 121 behind Marcus and the best part of a whole other league away. Mateta, Sesko, James and Mosquera all show 0 for GW6 on his squad sheet, so at least the zeros have each other for company. The only good news is that none of GW7's ten fixtures has kicked off yet, so he has a full eleven still to disappoint us with.

Brighton's Pascal Struijk has had his red card at Sunderland overturned on appeal, BBC Sport reports, so he dodges the one-match ban and is available for the visit of Crystal Palace this weekend. He was sent off after 57 minutes on a VAR call for denying Wilson Isidor, and Brighton still won 2-0. Marcus (De Cuyper, Kostoulas), Justin (Vuskovic) and Big Ben (Gross) all own Brighton players and keep their defence at full strength for GW7.

source.title: Struijk red card after VAR intervention overturned

items.text: BBC Sport argues the three-week break did Chelsea more good than anyone: Xabi Alonso reworked a back three that had shipped a league-high 12 goals before the pause, Moises Caicedo returned from his calf problem, and the 5-1 win over Bournemouth followed. Joao Pedro, who scored twice, said the break gave them time to fix the mistakes from the 3-0 loss at Brentford. Edward owns Palmer, Marcus has Joao Pedro and Big Ben has Rogers, and Chelsea go to Everton at 11:30 on Saturday.

source.title: Did Chelsea benefit most from extended international break?

items.text: Lisandro Martinez publicly questioned Manchester United's summer recruitment after the 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid, telling CBS "we don't have the best squad at the moment compared to other top teams" and "I expect more from our technical director", BBC Sport reports. Director of football Jason Wilcox is the target again. Robert (Yoro, Sesko), Marcus (Mbeumo), Small Ben (Cunha) and Big Ben (Bruno Fernandes) all have United players, and United are at Leeds on Saturday.

source.title: Wilcox the target again in another damaging Man Utd fallout

items.text: Marcus started GW6 ten points behind Edward and finished it 28 clear, a 38-point swing built on 77 to Edward's 39. De Cuyper 15, Dewsbury-Hall 13 and Joao Pedro 12 supplied 40 of them, and a left-back on 15 is the sort of thing people call luck right up until he is in their own team.

Robert was 89 behind the leader when GW6 began and is 121 behind now, having scored 35, exactly what Small Ben and Big Ben scored. Thirty-two points of ground gone in a week on a perfectly respectable return is the first thing to recede that fast in that part of the league since his hairline.

Small Ben began GW6 13 points off the top and ended it 45 off, with Cunha on 10, Donnarumma on 9 and Rice on 7 not nearly enough to stop it. For a man who is always looking up at somebody, the leader is now a very long way up.

Lisandro Martinez has apologised and been fined by Manchester United after criticising the club's hierarchy following the Atletico Madrid defeat, BBC Sport reports. He met the club's leadership and Michael Carrick on Thursday and said he spoke out of frustration. It remains to be seen whether Carrick picks him for Leeds on Sunday at 14:00 BST. Robert has Yoro, Ben D has Bruno Fernandes, Small Ben has Cunha and Marcus has Mbeumo, so four of the six have a stake in how this dressing room feels.

source.title: Martinez apologises for outburst and fined by Man Utd

items.text: The Guardian's weekend preview picks out Jordan Henderson, who at 36 became the oldest player to contribute directly to three goals in a Premier League game against Bournemouth, as the man who may dictate Chelsea's trip to unbeaten Everton. His partnership with Moises Caicedo is what lets Morgan Rogers, Joao Pedro and Cole Palmer flourish: Rogers is Big Ben's, Joao Pedro is Marcus's and Palmer is Edward's. Everton's defence, in the Guardian's words, littered the draw at Hull with costly mistakes, and Tarkowski, Branthwaite and Pickford belong to Edward, Big Ben and Justin.

source.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend

items.text: Gonzalo Garcia has one league goal from 18 shots this season and has not scored since his debut against Chelsea, the Guardian notes ahead of bottom club Fulham hosting Hull City. Fulham have six goals in six games and head coach Alvaro Arbeloa is under increasing pressure. Garcia is Big Ben's, and on the Guardian's numbers his expected goals tally of 3.60 says the finishing is due to turn.

source.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend

runs.note: 14:00 UTC (15:00 BST) slot: BHA v ARS, EVE v IPS, NEW v HUL. Confirmed NEW lineup found at newcastleunited.com. BHA, ARS, EVE, IPS and HUL sheets not available at a permitted outlet in time.
16:30 slot: NFO v COV. NFO confirmed XI found at skysports.com. COV sheet not needed (no league-owned players).

evening wrap: led with Arsenal's 3-0 loss at Brighton (ESPN) and Everton's 1-0 win over 10-man Ipswich with the Fatawu red card (ESPN), both tying into league squads. Opinions: Edward's overtake into 1st off Tarkowski/Barry/Garner, Small Ben's Newcastle stack, Justin's bench tying his XI 19-19 with big names blanking. Rewrote today's 13 FLOP lines via reflop.py. Both unused roast-archive suggestions passed over, not held for later: one targets sexuality, the other frames a real historical atrocity as a personal accusation - both fall outside the protected-categories rule regardless of who submitted them.

morning news, 4 fixtures today (BOU-LIV, LEE-CRY, MCI-SUN, FUL-MUN). Led with Odegaard's MCL knee injury (Edward) and Rice's back injury forcing him off at half-time (Ben C), then Foden's suspension for today's City-Sunderland game plus Reinildo's own ban (both touch Marcus), then Liverpool's clean bill of health ahead of Bournemouth (Ben C's four-man Liverpool stack). No opinion pieces on a morning run. Couldn't get a permitted source through Man Utd's Cloudflare wall for Fulham team news, so left that out rather than cite an aggregator.

13:00 slot: confirmed BOU-LIV and MCI-SUN sheets via Sky Sports live blogs (read as raw page data, not search snippets) - all league-owned starters at those four clubs listed, Foden (Marcus) and O'Reilly (Robert) the only ones left out. LEE-CRY sheet was not out at any permitted outlet by kick-off minus ~45 (tried leedsunited.com, cpfc.co.uk, Sky Sports live blog - lineup was image-only graphic with no extractable text); leedsunited.com's own preview did confirm Wilson (Robert) ruled out with a quad injury, so included that fact and left the rest of Leeds/Palace out of the counts rather than guess. BBC domains were unreachable from this session's fetcher throughout.

15:30 KO FUL v MUN: confirmed both squads via Sky Sports teams page (read as raw page data, id 6387779637306466232).
